name: Ging
description: Ging, also called Seven Cards, is a 17th-century English declaration gambling game for four players using a 28-card stripped pack, where players claim counters for most suit points or sweeping special combinations.
deck: Custom 28-card pack (K Q J 10 9 8 7 in each suit)

overview.description: Ging, also called Seven Cards, is a 17th-century English declaration gambling game for four players using a 28-card stripped pack, where players claim counters for most suit points or sweeping special combinations.
overview.deck: Custom 28-card pack (K Q J 10 9 8 7 in each suit)

history.origins: Ging is known from Francis Willughby's 17th-century game collection and is also referenced as Seven Cards.
timeline: 17th century: Recorded in Willughby's manuscript collection.
2003: Modern scholarly edition of Willughby's game book published.
2008: Playable reconstructed rules published for modern play.
history.cultural: The game reflects early English counter-stake gambling culture with precedence by elder hand and layout sweeps.
history.evolution: The available rules are reconstruction-oriented because no continuous living ruleset survived.

setup.players: 4 players clockwise, with eldest hand left of dealer and dealer as youngest hand.
setup.deck: 28 cards made by removing aces and cards below seven from a standard 52-card deck.
setup.dealing: Each player contributes two counters to dress the layout, then dealer gives 7 cards to each player clockwise.
setup.equipment: A square layout area and counters (chips).

rules.objective: Win counters from the central layout by best qualifying declaration in each deal.
rules.gameplay: There is no trick-play phase. After stake layout and deal, players evaluate hands and declare results. If no sweep combination is declared, counters are awarded for most of a suit and second most of a suit (court cards count 10, number cards by pip). Elder hand precedence breaks ties for most and second-most positions. If the same player holds both top suit totals, they take three corner counters. Five sweep combinations override suit-point awards, ranked highest to lowest: Seven Cards (all seven cards same suit), Four Sevens, Ging (a suit totaling exactly 37 with all cards held in that suit), Gentlemen (all face cards), Bare Shoulders (no face cards). A valid sweep takes all layout counters and the layout is re-dressed for next deal.
keyRules: Sweep declarations outrank and replace most-of-suit awards for that deal.
When multiple players qualify same combination, elder hand has priority.
Only one combination result is settled per deal based on precedence order.
Dealer rotates clockwise each deal; avoiding deal duty historically had a specific penalty.

strategy.basic: Check sweep conditions first because any valid sweep outranks suit-point outcomes.
strategy.intermediate: When no sweep exists, calculate all four suit totals quickly and resolve elder-hand tiebreaks accurately.
strategy.advanced: Maintain precise counter accounting around redressing to avoid payout mistakes in long sessions.
tips: Remember Ging requires exactly 37 in one suit and all cards held in that suit must be included in that total.
Do not miss rare combinations like bare shoulders while focusing on suit-point counting.

variations.name: Bankrupt End
variations.description: Session can end when a player loses their last counter; remaining layout is then divided as agreed.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Session-end rule only; no engine constant overrides needed for this variant.

variations.name: Fixed Number of Deals
variations.description: Alternative session structure plays a predetermined number of deals and splits pool at the end.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Session structure variant; no engine overrides required for this option.

scoring.description: Counters are won from a central layout either by highest declarations (most and second-most suit points) or by a full sweep combination.
scoring.winCondition: Session winner is determined by agreed endpoint, typically player with remaining or highest counters after agreed stop condition.

synthesis.shortDescription: Four-player counter game where special seven-card combinations can sweep the layout, otherwise best suit-point declarations win corner counters.
